parsed.why: Nationwide passport/visa marker regime with refusals and lifetime-fraud risk, enforced facilities bans in many states (criminal in four, one bathroom arrest), custody conversion practices and immigration abuse. Some states protective; measured measures partly enjoined.

No criminalisation; hate-speech, aggravating-factor and conversion bans on paper, but enforcement inconsistent (clergy incitement, uninvestigated attacks), no gender-identity discrimination ground, no recognition law. Conservative society: friction and underreporting, thin trans-specific recourse.

Working protection: gender-identity discrimination remedy with damages awarded, hate-crime law covering identity, no facilities bans, lived-gender custody standards. Deductions for organised exclusionary campaigns, patchy state coverage, one state's youth-care restrictions.

Never criminalised; state tolerates or ignores unless seen as immodest or campaigning, and trans people appear in temple/ceremonial life. But no protections, no recourse, media/assembly crackdowns, dated thin record of societal prejudice.

Explicit cross-dressing offence (six years) plus live morality statute; documented arrests, prosecutor-ordered anal exams, assembly bans and rising violence in the capital. Courts trend tolerant and assembly ban was frozen, but no remedy.
